finding.title: Occurrence uniqueness counts literal substrings inside longer leaf text, which the owner check does not reject
finding.evidence: Lines 52-59 accept an owner only when the p/li has exactly one #text child, trimHtmlSpace(text) === literal, and the raw inner slice also equals literal. Line 62-64, however, counts occurrences of `literal` in every in-body, non-unsafe #text node, including those in subtrees that line 51 does not skip. So a leaf whose text is only partly the literal (e.g. 'Updated daily at noon') contributes an occurrence and makes occurrences > 1, which fails the else branch at line 68-69. This is fail-closed. It does not create unsafe promotion. The only effect is that a valid exact owner is withheld when the same literal also appears as a substring of other non-owner text.
finding.reproduction:
Unexecuted reasoning trace. files menu.html = '

Updated daily

Updated daily at noon.

'; plan() with visible_copy 'Updated daily'; citation = exact owner '

Updated daily

'. locateOwner counts: the exact owner contributes one occurrence, and the second leaf's 'Updated daily' substring contributes another. occurrences === 2 gives {kind:'unwitnessed', reason:'literal_missing_or_not_unique'}. The delivery-assessment.ts:354-361 path then keeps the older unknown business disposition instead of the affirmative source fact.
finding.suggestion: Nothing changes for safety. If the intent is to let an exact owner witness the fact even when the same literal appears only as a substring elsewhere (not as another owner), consider counting exact simple p/li leaf texts (matching lines 52-56 rules) rather than every in-body #text substring, and keep the owners.length === 1 requirement unchanged. Otherwise, document this narrowing in the module comment.

post.reason: Exact owner plus any other safe body occurrence, even in a longer substring, stays unwitnessed. This is the deliberate unique-safe-occurrence gate; countertest preserves the narrowing. No unsafe promotion shown.
